summary: Source-side config verification for iOS Critical Alerts (bug: quake-ed6916e5-... APNs returned 200 but phone did not wake/play sound). All 4 checks PASS at the source level, so the source inputs feeding the EAS build are correct. Since APNs already returned 200 with the correct payload, the most likely remaining root cause lives on the OUTPUT side of the pipeline (IPA / provisioning profile / device settings), not the source.

1_siren_caf_present.note: Valid Core Audio Format (CAF) file — first 4 bytes are 'caff' as required by Apple's CAF spec. Regular file, not symlink.

2_app_json_plugin_sounds.note: expo-notifications plugin has sounds array containing exactly './assets/audio/siren.caf'. This is what triggers Expo prebuild to copy siren.caf into iOS bundle Library/Sounds/ at EAS build time.

2_app_json_ios_entitlements.note: Both required entitlements are declared. Note: presence in app.json only *requests* the entitlement from Apple during EAS build; whether the final provisioning profile carries com.apple.developer.usernotifications.critical-alerts can only be confirmed by inspecting the built IPA's embedded.mobileprovision (not accessible from this sandbox).

4_no_regression_from_test_agent.note: No files were modified during this verification run — read-only static + one direct import of _build_critical_payload.

action_items: Since all 4 source-side inputs are correct and APNs itself returned 200 with the exact expected payload, the failure to wake/sound the phone is almost certainly on the OUTPUT side of the pipeline. Recommended next diagnostics (require the built IPA or the device):

A) Inspect the actual IPA (1.0.14/build 1013): unzip Payload/QuakeGuard.app and verify siren.caf exists at Library/Sounds/siren.caf (or bundle root). If missing, EAS prebuild did not honour the plugin sounds array for that build — bump app.json version, clear EAS cache, rebuild.

B) Extract embedded.mobileprovision from the IPA and run `security cms -D -i embedded.mobileprovision | plutil -p -` — confirm the Entitlements dict contains 'com.apple.developer.usernotifications.critical-alerts' = true. If absent, the provisioning profile was regenerated by EAS without the entitlement — request a new profile in Apple Developer portal that includes Critical Alerts, then rebuild.

C) On-device check (Settings > Notifications > QuakeGuard): confirm 'Critical Alerts' toggle is ON. Even with entitlement + correct payload, iOS suppresses critical audio if user has not granted the Critical Alerts permission at first-run. Verify the app calls requestPermissionsAsync with ios.allowCriticalAlerts: true.

D) MINOR: /app/frontend/app.json version is '1.0.8' but user says built IPA is '1.0.14/build 1013'. Either the checked-in version drifted from what was actually shipped to EAS, or version/buildNumber are being overridden by eas.json / EAS remote versioning. Confirm which app.json+eas.json snapshot produced build 1013 — a divergent snapshot could have shipped without the plugin sounds entry or without the entitlements.
critical_code_review_comments: apns.py _build_critical_payload is correctly structured for iOS Critical Alerts: sound is a dict (not string), critical=1, volume<=1.0, interruption-level=critical, priority=10 header (line 246), apns-push-type=alert (line 245). No source-side defects found.
context_for_next_testing_agent: This iteration was source-only static verification for iOS Critical Alerts config. All 4 requested checks PASS. Root cause of silent-phone bug is NOT in /app source — it must be verified against the built IPA (bundle contents + embedded.mobileprovision entitlements) and/or on-device Critical Alerts permission. Sandbox cannot download the IPA from EAS servers.
rca_of_issue: Not fully determinable from source alone. Source config is correct (siren.caf present + valid CAF, app.json plugin sounds entry present, both iOS entitlements declared, APNs payload structure correct). Given APNs returned 200 for trigger quake-ed6916e5-5ae3-4283-92a7-3e9c5e08ee80 with the exact expected payload, the fault is downstream of the source: either (a) EAS build 1013 did not bundle siren.caf into Library/Sounds/ (so iOS falls back silently and doesn't honour critical semantics), (b) EAS regenerated the provisioning profile without the com.apple.developer.usernotifications.critical-alerts entitlement (so iOS strips critical semantics before playback), or (c) the user has not granted the runtime Critical Alerts permission on the device. The Apple Watch pinging silently while the phone stayed asleep is the fingerprint of scenario (a) or (b) — the push was accepted and forwarded to the Watch as a generic notification, but the phone-side critical-alert override was rejected.
